sn3.1:1.3: Pasenadi, son of Sañjaya Mahākosala, ruled the nation of Kosala from its capital Sāvatthī until his death shortly before the Buddha. Like the Buddha’s family, he claimed descent from the Solar lineage of Okkāka. He features throughout the Suttas as a well-meaning if sometimes naive ruler.
sn3.1:1.4: Pasenadi’s polite but not reverential behavior indicates that he is not yet a devotee of the Buddha. This may, in fact, record their first meeting.
sn3.1:2.2: The sequence of names here differs from the usual.
sn3.1:8.2: This is an allusion to the venomous bite, _tejas_ having roots in both “sharp” and “fiery”. This metaphor is the origin of the dragon’s fiery breath.
sn3.1:12.3: PTS dict gives this ref for pasu = cattle and pasava = offspring.
sn3.1:12.6: BB gives the doctrinally correct Buddhist explanation for this. But as it stands, the text reads as if the mendicant is exacting fiery vengeance with their psychic power.
